findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.

No 'acl' attribute is set and no public access block is configured, leaving the bucket subject to the account/bucket default ACL which may allow unintended access; combined with no encryption this increases exposure risk for a bucket that also holds an uploaded object.
The bucket stores financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook data unencrypted at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recourse, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irrecoverable data loss if access controls are ever bypassed or misused, and indicates weak protective defaults for sensitive data buckets.

The object is uploaded to a bucket (reports_archive) that lacks server-side encryption configuration and no per-object server_side_encryption/kms key is specified, so this file is stored without encryption at rest.
